title: Men are More Likely than Women to Slow in the Marathon
claims: The analysis covered 91,929 marathon performances across 14 United States marathons in 2011, comparing pace change from start to finish.
Runners were classified as maintaining pace when slowing was under 10%, and as marked slowers when slowing reached or exceeded 30%.
Mean pace change was about 15.6% for men and 11.7% for women, showing that progressive slowing through the latter half is common rather than exceptional.
